provisions.policy_name: Removal of D/S for F, J, and I nonimmigrants
provisions.current_rule: Use of Duration of Status (D/S) for these nonimmigrants
provisions.proposed_rule: Striking all references to D/S for F, J, and I nonimmigrants
provisions.plain_english: References to Duration of Status will be removed for F, J, and I visa holders.
restrictions: No use of D/S for F, J, and I nonimmigrants
provisions.evidence_quote: Striking all references to D/S for F, J, and I nonimmigrants;

provisions.policy_name: Fixed time admission and EOS procedure for F, J, and I nonimmigrants
provisions.proposed_rule: Describing requirements for F and J nonimmigrants seeking admission, including after travel abroad and those approved for OPT and academic training; Updating cross references and clarifying standards for admission in the automatic extension visa validity provisions that cover F and J nonimmigrants applying at a POE after an absence not exceeding 30 days solely in a contiguous territory or adjacent islands; Outlining the process for EOS applications for F, J, and I nonimmigrants; Providing a short-term reprieve from filing for EOS during the first 6 months after the rule takes effect if applying for employment authorization for either post-completion OPT or STEM OPT; Specifying the effect of departure while an F, J, or I nonimmigrant's application for an EOS and/or employment authorization is pending; Providing procedures specific to the transition from D/S to admission for a fixed time period of authorized stay for these nonimmigrants; Codifying that an F-1 student who has timely filed an EOS application will be authorized to continue full course of study after admission period expiration until USCIS adjudicates the EOS application.
provisions.plain_english: Admission and extension of stay for F, J, and I visa holders will have fixed time periods with an outlined process for extension and protections for timely filers.
requirements: Requirements for F and J admissions
EOS procedures for F, J, and I nonimmigrants
Timely EOS filing to continue study
restrictions: Departure affects pending EOS or employment authorization applications
exceptions: Short-term reprieve for post-completion OPT or STEM OPT workers in first 6 months of rule implementation
time_limits_or_durations: 30 day absence rule for automatic extension
provisions.evidence_quote: Describing requirements for F and J nonimmigrants seeking admission, including after travel abroad and those approved for OPT and academic training; Updating the cross reference and clarifying the standards for admission in the automatic extension visa validity provisions that cover F and J nonimmigrants applying at a Port of Entry (POE) after an absence not exceeding 30 days solely in a contiguous territory or adjacent islands; Outlining the process for EOS applications for F, J, and I nonimmigrants; Providing a short-term reprieve from filing for EOS during the first 6 months after the rule takes effect if applying for employment authorization for either post-completion OPT or STEM OPT; Specifying the effect of departure while an F, J, or I nonimmigrant's application for an EOS in F, J, or I nonimmigrant status and/or employment authorization (and an associated employment authorization document (EAD)) is pending; Providing procedures specific to the transition from D/S to admission for a fixed time period of authorized stay for F, J, and I nonimmigrants; Codifying that an F-1 student who has timely filed an EOS application, will be authorized to continue pursuing a full course of study after the expiration of the admission period until USCIS adjudicates the EOS application.

provisions.policy_name: Setting authorized admission and extension periods for F and J nonimmigrants
provisions.proposed_rule: Setting the authorized admission and extension periods for F and J nonimmigrants up to the program length, not to exceed a 4-year period
provisions.plain_english: F and J visa holders can be admitted or extended for up to the length of their program, but no more than 4 years.
requirements: Admissions/extensions limited to program length up to 4 years
provisions.evidence_quote: Setting the authorized admission and extension periods for F and J nonimmigrants up to the program length, not to exceed a 4-year period;

provisions.policy_name: Require F-1 students to complete first academic year at initial school before transfer or change in educational objective
affected_groups: F-1 students transferring schools or changing educational objectives
provisions.proposed_rule: For F-1 students changing educational objectives or transferring to an SEVP-certified school, requiring that the student complete his or her first academic year of a program of study at the school that initially issued his or her Form I-20 or successor form, unless an exception is authorized by SEVP
provisions.plain_english: F-1 students must finish their first academic year at their original school before transferring or changing educational goals, unless SEVP allows an exception.
requirements: Complete first academic year at initial school
provisions.evidence_quote: For F-1 students changing educational objectives or transferring to an SEVP-certified school, requiring that the student complete his or her first academic year of a program of study at the school that initially issued his or her Form I-20 or successor form, unless an exception is authorized by SEVP;

provisions.policy_name: Prohibit graduate-level F-1 students from changing educational objectives or transferring without exception
affected_groups: Graduate level or above F-1 students
provisions.proposed_rule: Prohibiting F-1 students at the graduate education level or above from changing educational objectives at any point during a program of study; Prohibiting such students from transferring during their program unless an exception is authorized by SEVP for extenuating circumstances
provisions.plain_english: Graduate-level F-1 students cannot change their educational goals or transfer schools during their program unless SEVP grants an exception for extenuating circumstances.
requirements: No changes in objectives or transfers unless SEVP authorizes exception
restrictions: Prohibition on changes and transfers during program for graduate students
exceptions: Exception authorized by SEVP for extenuating circumstances
provisions.evidence_quote: Prohibiting F-1 students at the graduate education level or above from changing educational objectives at any point during a program of study; Prohibiting F-1 students at the graduate education level or above from transferring at any point during their program of study, unless an exception is authorized by SEVP for extenuating circumstances;

provisions.policy_name: Require F-1 nonimmigrants to begin higher education programs at higher levels only
provisions.proposed_rule: Requiring any nonimmigrant who has completed a program at one educational level to only be allowed to begin another program at a higher educational level as an F-1 student and prohibiting a change to the same or a lower educational level while an F-1 student
provisions.plain_english: F-1 students can only start a new program at a higher education level after completing one; they can't move to the same or lower level.
requirements: Must begin new program at higher level only
restrictions: No change to same or lower educational level allowed
provisions.evidence_quote: Requiring any nonimmigrant who has completed a program at one educational level to only be allowed to begin another program at a higher educational level as an F-1 student and prohibiting a change to the same or a lower educational level while an F-1 student;

provisions.policy_name: Decrease grace period for F-1 nonimmigrants after program or training completion
provisions.proposed_rule: Decreasing the period allowed for F-1 nonimmigrants to prepare to depart from the U.S. after completion of a course of study or authorized post-completion practical training from 60 to 30 days; Requiring departure or action to maintain lawful status within 30 days if study or training ends early
provisions.plain_english: F-1 students now have 30 days (instead of 60) to prepare to leave the U.S. after finishing their program or training, and must leave or maintain status within 30 days if they end early.
requirements: Depart U.S. or maintain lawful status within 30 days after course completion or early end
provisions.evidence_quote: Decreasing the period allowed for F-1 nonimmigrants to prepare to depart from the United States after completion of a course of study or an authorized period of post-completion practical training from 60 to 30 days; Requiring that if an F-1 student ends study or training early, the student and eligible dependents must depart the U.S. or take action to maintain lawful status within 30 days of the end date;

provisions.policy_name: Provide for biometric collection for EOS applications
provisions.proposed_rule: Providing for collection of biometric information in conjunction with an EOS application for F, J, and I nonimmigrants as may be required by 8 CFR 103.16
provisions.plain_english: Biometric data may be collected when F, J, or I visa holders file extension of stay applications.
requirements: Biometric info collection with EOS applications
provisions.evidence_quote: Providing for collection of biometric information in conjunction with an EOS application for F, J, and I nonimmigrants as may be required by 8 CFR 103.16;

provisions.policy_name: Limit language training students to 24 months aggregate period of stay
provisions.proposed_rule: Limiting language training students to an aggregate 24-month period of stay, including breaks and an annual vacation
provisions.plain_english: Students in language training programs can stay for no more than 24 months total including breaks.
requirements: Maximum 24 months aggregate stay
provisions.evidence_quote: Limiting language training students to an aggregate 24-month period of stay, including breaks and an annual vacation;

provisions.policy_name: Disallow program extensions for delays caused by academic probation or repeated inability to complete program
provisions.proposed_rule: Providing that a delay in completing one's program by the program end date, including delays caused by academic probation or suspension or a student's repeated inability or unwillingness to complete course of study, is generally an unacceptable reason for program extensions for F nonimmigrants
provisions.plain_english: Extending the program due to academic probation, suspension, or failure to complete studies is usually not allowed.
restrictions: No extensions for delays caused by academic probation, suspension, or inability/unwillingness to complete studies
provisions.evidence_quote: Providing that a delay in completing one's program by the program end date specified on the Form I-20, which includes but is not limited to delays caused by academic probation or suspension or a student's repeated inability or unwillingness to complete his or her course of study, is generally an unacceptable reason for program extensions for F nonimmigrants;

provisions.policy_name: Auto-extension of employment authorization for F nonimmigrants with severe economic hardship
affected_groups: F nonimmigrants with pending timely filed EOS applications
provisions.proposed_rule: Allowing F nonimmigrants whose timely filed EOS applications remain pending after their admission period has expired to receive an auto-extension of current authorization for on-campus and off-campus employment based on severe economic hardship resulting from emergent circumstances under existing 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(v). The auto-extension will be up to 240 days or the end date of the Federal Register notice announcing suspension of certain regulatory requirements, whichever is earlier.
provisions.plain_english: F students waiting for extension approval can automatically extend work authorization for up to 240 days if facing serious economic hardship.
requirements: Timely filed EOS application
Severe economic hardship from emergent circumstances
restrictions: Auto-extension limited to 240 days or Federal Register suspension end date
provisions.evidence_quote: Allowing F nonimmigrants whose timely filed EOS applications remain pending after their admission period has expired to receive an auto-extension of their current authorization for on-campus and off-campus employment based on severe economic hardship resulting from emergent circumstances under existing 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(v). The length of the auto-extension of employment authorization will be up to 240 days or the end date of the Federal Register notice announcing the suspension of certain regulatory requirements, whichever is earlier;

provisions.policy_name: Limiting I nonimmigrants admission to fixed time period not exceeding 240 days
provisions.current_rule: Duration of Status (D/S) applies to I nonimmigrants
provisions.proposed_rule: Replacing D/S for I nonimmigrants with admission for a fixed time period until they complete activities or assignments consistent with the I classification, not to exceed 240 days (except some I nonimmigrants from PRC), with an EOS available for those meeting specified requirements
provisions.plain_english: I visa holders will have fixed admission periods up to 240 days; extensions of stay are allowed under conditions; shorter terms apply for PRC nationals.
requirements: Admission limited to fixed period not exceeding 240 days
EOS available if requirements met
restrictions: Max 240 days except some PRC I nonimmigrants
exceptions: Some Chinese PRC nationals max 90 days work extension
time_limits_or_durations: 90 days for some PRC I nonimmigrants
provisions.evidence_quote: Replacing D/S for I nonimmigrants with admission for a fixed time period until they complete the activities or assignments consistent with the I classification, not to exceed 240 days (with the exception of some I nonimmigrants from the PRC), with an EOS available for I nonimmigrants who can meet specified EOS requirements;

provisions.policy_name: Codifying definition and evidence for I nonimmigrant foreign media organizations
provisions.proposed_rule: Codifying the definition of a foreign media organization for I nonimmigrant status, consistent with USCIS and DoS practice; Updating the evidence an alien must submit to demonstrate eligibility for the I classification
provisions.plain_english: Officially defining foreign media organizations for I visa eligibility and updating evidence requirements.
requirements: Submit updated evidence demonstrating I classification eligibility
provisions.evidence_quote: Codifying the definition of a foreign media organization for I nonimmigrant status, consistent with long-standing U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) and U.S. Department of State (DoS) practice; Updating the evidence an alien must submit to demonstrate eligibility for the I nonimmigrant classification;

provisions.policy_name: Continue work authorization for J-1 nonimmigrants with specific employer up to 240 days pending EOS
affected_groups: J-1 nonimmigrants with employment authorization incident to status
provisions.current_rule: Work authorization linked to status expiration without automatic extension longer than existing provisions
provisions.proposed_rule: Clarifying that J-1 nonimmigrants employment authorized with a specific employer incident to status continue to be authorized for up to 240 days under existing 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(20) if status expires while timely filed EOS application is pending; J-2 dependents applying for employment authorization via EAD do not have continued work authorization once EAD expires
provisions.plain_english: J-1 workers can continue working for up to 240 days if their extension is pending, but their J-2 dependents cannot if their work authorization expires.
requirements: Timely filed EOS application
Employment authorization incident to status for J-1
restrictions: J-2 dependents lose work authorization after EAD expiration
provisions.evidence_quote: Clarifying that J-1 nonimmigrants who are employment authorized with a specific employer incident to status continue to be authorized for such employment for up to 240 days under the existing regulatory provision at 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(20) if their status expires while their timely filed EOS application is pending, whereas J-2 dependents, who must apply for employment authorization as evidenced by an EAD, do not have the benefit of continued work authorization once the EAD expires;

provisions.policy_name: Temporary reprieve for J-1s with D/S expiration allowing EOS filing and continued work
affected_groups: J-1 nonimmigrants whose D/S expires shortly after rule takes effect
provisions.proposed_rule: Providing a temporary reprieve for J-1s whose D/S expires shortly after the rule takes effect by allowing them to apply for EOS and continue to work for the duration on their new Form DS-2019 regardless of how long the EOS adjudication takes
provisions.plain_english: J-1 visa holders with soon-expiring D/S can file for extension and work for the entire new program period even if extension adjudication is delayed.
requirements: Ability to file EOS application
Continuation of work authorization during processing
exceptions: Limited to those expiring shortly after rule effective date
provisions.evidence_quote: Providing a temporary reprieve for those J-1s whose D/S status expires shortly after the rule takes effect by allowing them to apply for EOS and continue to work for the duration of the time on their new Form DS-2019 regardless of how long the EOS application takes to adjudicate;

provisions.policy_name: Require J-1 exchange visitors and dependents to depart or maintain status within 30 days if program end date shortens
provisions.proposed_rule: Requiring that if the program end date is shortened, J-1 exchange visitors and any J-2 dependents must leave the U.S. within 30 days from the new program end date or otherwise seek to maintain lawful status in that 30-day period
provisions.plain_english: If J-1 program ends earlier than expected, the J-1 and dependents have 30 days to depart or maintain lawful status.
requirements: Depart or maintain lawful status within 30 days of shortened program end date
provisions.evidence_quote: Requiring that if the program end date is shortened, the J-1 exchange visitor and any J-2 accompanying dependents must leave the United States within 30 days from the new program end date or otherwise seek to maintain lawful status in that 30-day period;

provisions.policy_name: Responsibilities of Responsible Officer (RO) for late program extension requests
provisions.proposed_rule: Providing the responsibilities of the responsible officer when submitting late requests for extension of current program end date for exchange visitors
provisions.plain_english: Clear rules on what ROs must do if they file late extension requests for exchange visitors’ program end dates.
requirements: Responsible officer must fulfill specified responsibilities for late extension requests
provisions.evidence_quote: Providing the responsibilities of the responsible officer (RO) when submitting late requests for extension of current program end date for exchange visitors;

provisions.policy_name: Allow I nonimmigrants to work up to 240 days (90 days for PRC) pending EOS application
provisions.proposed_rule: Clarifying that I nonimmigrants are authorized to continue working in the U.S. for their foreign employer under 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(20) for up to 240 days (except I nonimmigrants from the PRC who may continue working for up to 90 days) while their timely filed EOS application is pending
provisions.plain_english: I visa holders can continue working up to 240 days while extension is pending; PRC nationals get up to 90 days.
requirements: Timely filed EOS application
provisions.evidence_quote: Clarifying that I nonimmigrants are authorized to continue working in the United States for their foreign employer, under 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(20), for up to 240 days (with the exception of I nonimmigrants from the PRC who may continue working for up to 90 days) while their timely filed EOS application is pending;

provisions.policy_name: Strike all references to 'duration of status' or 'duration of employment' for F, J, and I classifications
provisions.current_rule: Use of duration of status or duration of employment terminology
provisions.proposed_rule: Striking all references to 'duration of status' and/or 'duration of employment' for the F, J, and I nonimmigrant classifications
provisions.plain_english: All mentions of 'duration of status' or 'duration of employment' are removed for F, J, and I visa categories.
restrictions: No references to duration of status or employment
provisions.evidence_quote: Striking all references to ``duration of status'' and/or ``duration of employment'' for the F, J, and I nonimmigrant classifications;

provisions.policy_name: Including severability clause in the final rule
affected_groups: All affected nonimmigrants and DHS implementation
provisions.proposed_rule: Including a severability clause so if any provision of the rule is not implemented, remaining provisions can still be implemented
provisions.plain_english: If part of this rule isn’t implemented, the rest can still be put into effect.
provisions.evidence_quote: Including a severability clause. In the event that any provision of this rule is not implemented for whatever reason, the remaining provisions can be implemented in accordance with the stated purposes of this rule.

provisions.policy_name: Limiting ability to delay or suspend implementation of provisions 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(ii)(A)-(C) to two years
affected_groups: F, J nonimmigrants subject to 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(ii)(A)-(C)
provisions.current_rule: Indefinite ability to delay or suspend implementation of these provisions
provisions.proposed_rule: Amending 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(ii)(E) to limit the ability to delay or suspend implementation of 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(ii)(A) through (C) for two years from the effective date of the rule
provisions.plain_english: Delays or suspensions of certain regulatory provisions can only last two years, not indefinitely.
restrictions: Delay/suspension limited to two years from rule effective date
provisions.evidence_quote: Amending 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(ii)(E) to limit the ability to delay or suspend the implementation of 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(ii)(A) through (C) for a period of two years from the effective date of the rule since this provision is not needed indefinitely.

provisions.policy_name: Rules for F or J nonimmigrants changing status before effective date and seeking admission after
affected_groups: F nonimmigrants with pre-rule change of status approvals
provisions.proposed_rule: Establishing requirements to determine the period of stay for F or J nonimmigrants whose change of status application was approved before the final rule's effective date and who depart the U.S. then seek admission after the final rule's effective date
provisions.plain_english: New rules define their period of authorized stay for F or J visa holders approved before the rule who travel abroad and return after the rule takes effect.
requirements: Determine period of stay according to new requirements upon re-admission
provisions.evidence_quote: Establishing requirements to determine the period of stay for F or J nonimmigrants whose change of status application was approved before the final rule's effective date and who depart the United States, then seek admission after the final rule's effective date;

provisions.policy_name: Deeming change of status applications abandoned upon departure
affected_groups: Aliens with pending change of status applications, including F or J status
provisions.proposed_rule: Codifying the policy that DHS deems abandoned any application to change to another nonimmigrant status, including F or J status, if the alien who timely filed the application departs the U.S. while the application is pending
provisions.plain_english: If someone leaves the U.S. while their change of status request is pending, DHS will treat the application as abandoned.
restrictions: Departure during pending application causes abandonment
provisions.evidence_quote: Codifying the long-standing policy under which DHS deems abandoned an application to change to another nonimmigrant status, including F or J status, if the alien who timely filed the application departs the United States while the application is pending.

provisions.policy_name: Update employment authorization provisions to align with revisions in 8 CFR 214.2
affected_groups: F, J, I nonimmigrants authorized to accept employment
provisions.current_rule: Existing employment authorization provisions prior to revision
provisions.proposed_rule: Amending 8 CFR 274a.12 to incorporate the revisions in 8 CFR 214.2 regarding employment authorization
provisions.plain_english: Updating employment authorization rules to reflect changes made in visa admission and extension provisions.
provisions.evidence_quote: Amending 8 CFR 274a.12, Classes of aliens authorized to accept employment, by updating the employment authorization provisions to incorporate the revisions in 8 CFR 214.2.
